_comment: Curated Items. Authoring conventions (converted by scripts/build_db.py): years are HISTORICAL (negative = BCE, no year 0); 'from_unc'/'to_unc' = +/- years for circa values; 'from_ka'/'to_ka' = thousands of years before 1950; 'date'/'date_to' = ISO-like historical dates (e.g. '-0196-03-27'). 'ev' tokens: 'wp:<English Wikipedia title>' (revision id resolved from data/seed/wikipedia_evidence.json), 'wd' (Wikidata item), or a source_id. An item-level 'ev' is the default evidence for its facets. Coordinates, countries, admin areas and Wikidata dates are NOT authored here: they are imported from the raw Wikidata snapshot. 'wd_review' annotates imported Wikidata claims (status/note) without deleting them.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
items.description: Largest of the Giza pyramids; tomb built for the Fourth Dynasty king Khufu.

time.label: between 2700 and 2500 BC
time.note: Range of 'the majority of recent chronological estimates' for Khufu and his pyramid (Wikipedia).

time.label: 2871–2604 BC (calibrated, mortar charcoal)
time.note: Radiocarbon dates on organic inclusions in mortar; charcoal can carry an old-wood offset.

time.label: completion 2620–2484 BC (reanalysis)
time.note: Reanalysis based on the younger samples, as reported by Wikipedia. The underlying study (Bonani et al. 2001, Radiocarbon) was located via OpenAlex but its abstract states no values: not verified at source.

time.label: the tomb of King Khufu (c. 2589–2566 BC); an estimated 10 to 20 years to build
time.note: Official page gives Khufu's reign; construction is placed within that reign. Institutional statement following one conventional chronology.

attrs.note: 'an estimated 10 to 20 years to build' (official page).

items.name: Pyramid of Djoser
items.description: Step pyramid at Saqqara, the first Egyptian pyramid, built for the burial of Djoser.

time.label: 27th century BC
time.note: Built during the Third Dynasty, in the reign of Djoser (c. 2670–2650 BC per Wikipedia).

items.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
items.description: Colossal limestone sphinx on the Giza plateau; the king it represents and who commissioned it are disputed.

links.note: Archaeological evidence points to Khufu OR Khafre; no scholarly consensus (Wikipedia). Lehner (1991, abstract) attributes the quarrying of the Sphinx site to builders under Khafre (ca. 2,500 B.C.). Extra evidence for one side does not close the dispute.
Alternative attribution; Wikipedia gives Khufu (c. 2590–2566 BC) or Khafre (c. 2558–2532 BC).

time.label: under Khafre (ca. 2,500 B.C.)
time.note: Dating tied to the Khafre attribution.

P2596:Q634708.action: decide identity of Q634708 vs Q11768
P2596:Q634708.note: Wikidata has both 'culture of ancient Egypt' (Q634708) and 'Ancient Egypt' (Q11768); not auto-merged.

items.name: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62)
items.description: Rock-cut tomb in the Valley of the Kings, found largely intact in 1922.

time.label: burial c. 1323 BC
time.note: Derived from the end of Tutankhamun's reign (1332–1323 BC, Wikipedia); the burial date itself is inferred, not directly dated.

items.name: Karnak Temple Complex
items.description: Vast temple complex at Thebes, built and expanded over ~2,000 years.

time.label: from the reign of Senusret I (1971–1926 BCE) into the Ptolemaic Kingdom (305–30 BCE)
time.note: Four-bound example: start known to within a reign, end known only to within a dynasty.

items.name: Abu Simbel temples
items.description: Twin rock-cut temples of Ramesses II in Nubia, relocated in the 1960s ahead of Lake Nasser.

links.note: Sculpture in the Great Temple commemorates Ramesses II at Kadesh.

time.label: completed around 1265 BC (year 24 of Ramesses II)
time.note: The same Wikipedia revision states both c. 1264–1244 BC and completion c. 1265 BC after ~20 years of work; kept as two claims rather than silently choosing.

time.label: relocation completed 1968
time.note: Start of the rescue operation not captured (unknown in this source extract).

items.name: Pyramids of Meroë
items.description: Royal Nubian pyramids of the Kingdom of Kush at Meroë (Sudan).

time.label: c. 280 BC (royal burials move to Meroë) – 4th century AD
time.note: Combines two statements: royal burial ground transferred to Meroë c. 280 BC; the kingdom collapsed in the 4th century AD.

items.name: Great Zimbabwe
items.description: Medieval stone-walled city, capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe.

time.label: settled from around 1000 AD
time.note: End of occupation not stated in the retrieved source: open-ended.

time.label: capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century
time.note: Only the start is bounded (13th century).

items.name: Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela
items.description: Monolithic churches carved from rock at Lalibela, Ethiopia.

P140:Q3333484.note: Wikidata lists 'Eastern Orthodoxy'; the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church belongs to Oriental Orthodoxy. Kept as a disputed claim, not deleted.

P276:Q863404.note: 'location: subterranea' — a generic concept (underground structures), not a place.

time.label: late 12th or early 13th century AD (dating given for the Church of Saint George)
time.note: Source dates the best-known church (Bete Giyorgis); applying it to the whole group is a curator generalisation. Wikidata inception (13th century) imported separately.

items.name: Blombos Cave
items.description: Middle Stone Age cave site with some of the earliest evidence of symbolic behaviour.

time.label: Still Bay sequence 75,500–67,800 years ago
time.note: Sub-phase estimate (2013), 95% confidence.

items.name: Stonehenge
items.description: Prehistoric monument of a stone circle within a henge, built in phases.

function.note: Deposits of human bone from c. 3000 BC onwards.
Solstitial alignment is accepted; its calendrical purpose is an interpretation.

time.label: phases from about 3100 BC to about 1600 BC
sarsen circle placed 2600–2400 BC
time.note: Phase-level extent (sarsen circle).

time.label: in about 2500 BC the stones were set up in the centre of the monument
earliest phase (circular bank and ditch) dated to about 3100 BC
earliest earthwork built about 3000 BC
time.note: Institutional rounded date; differs from the c. 3100 BC given by Wikipedia. Both kept.

time.label: central bluestones rearranged '200 or 300 years later' than c. 2500 BC
time.note: Derived arithmetic from the source's wording ('about 2500 BC' + '200 or 300 years later').

P149:Q435405.note: 'architectural style: prehistoric Britain' is a period/region, not a style; not imported.

items.name: Newgrange
items.description: Large Neolithic passage tomb in the Boyne valley, aligned to the winter-solstice sunrise.

time.label: 3000–2500 BC (later estimate)
time.note: 'Some put its period of construction somewhat later' (Wikipedia).

items.name: Carnac stones
items.description: Thousands of Neolithic standing stones in rows in Brittany.

time.label: probably around 3300 BC, some perhaps as early as 4500 BC
time.note: Start uncertain between 4500 and 3300 BC; most stones probably c. 3300 BC.

items.name: Ħaġar Qim
items.description: Megalithic temple complex on Malta (Ġgantija phase).

time.label: main temple built between 3600 and 3200 BC
time.note: Northern ruins are 'considerably older' (undated in source).

items.name: Dolmen of Menga
items.description: Neolithic megalithic burial mound (long-barrow dolmen) at Antequera.

items.name: Skara Brae
items.description: Stone-built Neolithic village on Orkney.

items.name: Lascaux
items.description: Cave with Upper Palaeolithic paintings, discovered in 1940.

culture.note: 'early Magdalenian' per Wikipedia; attribution has been debated.

time.label: paintings usually estimated at 17,000–22,000 years old
time.note: '17,000 to 22,000 years' old, stored as ka before 1950; the ~75-year difference between 'before 1950' and 'before today' is far below the precision.

items.name: Knossos
items.description: Neolithic-to-Roman settlement on Crete; site of the largest Minoan palace.

time.label: settlement from around 7000 BC into the modern period
time.note: Open-ended occupation.

time.label: palace: first built c. 1900 BC; major destruction conventionally c. 1350 BC
time.note: Final-destruction chronology 'remains debated' (Wikipedia).

items.name: Treasury of Atreus
items.description: Monumental tholos (beehive) tomb at Mycenae.

items.name: Akrotiri (Bronze Age settlement)
items.description: Bronze Age town on Santorini buried by the Minoan (Theran) eruption.

items.name: Parthenon
items.description: Doric temple of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis.

time.label: begun 447 BC, completed 438 BC, decoration until 432 BC
converted into a church in the final decade of the 6th century AD

items.name: Colosseum
items.description: Flavian amphitheatre in Rome.

time.label: begun c. 70–72 AD under Vespasian, completed AD 80 under Titus

items.name: Pompeii
items.description: Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE.

time.label: buried in 79 AD
time.note: The day is disputed; see event:vesuvius-79.

time.label: 6th-century BC necropolis and Etruscan inscriptions – 79 AD
time.note: Start inferred from excavated 6th-century BC necropolis.

items.name: Sutton Hoo
items.description: Anglo-Saxon burial ground with the Mound 1 ship burial.

links.note: 'Most likely' candidate according to scholars; not proven.

time.label: ship burial dated 610–635 by its Merovingian coins

items.name: Göbekli Tepe
items.description: Pre-Pottery Neolithic site with monumental T-pillar enclosures in Upper Mesopotamia.

function.note: 'No definitive purpose has been determined'; popularly called 'the world's first temple'.
Newer interpretation: inhabited settlement, replacing the 'nomad sanctuary' model.

time.label: inhabited from around 9500 BCE to at least 8000 BCE
time.note: Latest end left open: 'or perhaps slightly later'.

time.label: Layer II: late 9th / early 8th millennium calBC
time.note: Numeric bounds are a POC reading of 'late 9th / early 8th millennium' (reversible); the source wording is kept in the label.

items.name: Çatalhöyük
items.description: Large Neolithic and Chalcolithic proto-city in southern Anatolia.

items.name: Tell es-Sultan (Ancient Jericho)
items.description: Settlement mound of ancient Jericho with one of the earliest permanent settlements.

time.label: first permanent settlement between 10,000 and 9000 BCE (Natufian)
time.note: Open-ended occupation; later phases not modelled in the POC.

items.name: Tower of Jericho
items.description: Pre-Pottery Neolithic stone tower at Tell es-Sultan. Sub-structure example: has no own coordinates, inherits location via part_of.

function.note: Fortification theory (one of three main theories; the authors argue it is flawed).
Barkai & Liran's proposal: aligned to the midsummer sunset.

time.label: built around 8300 BCE, in use until c. 7800 BCE
wall and tower built around 8000 BCE
time.note: Two statements in the same source; the radiocarbon one is ranked preferred.

items.name: Ziggurat of Ur
items.description: Early Bronze Age ziggurat of the Third Dynasty of Ur, dedicated to Nanna.

time.label: 21st century BC (short chronology)
time.note: Depends on Mesopotamian chronology choice (short chronology).

items.name: Mohenjo-daro
items.description: Major city of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

time.label: built around 2500 BC; abandoned c. 1700 BCE

items.name: Persepolis
items.description: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.

links.note: Inscriptions support that the terrace and first palaces were built by Darius.

time.label: earliest remains date to 515 BC; extended under Xerxes I, Artaxerxes I and in the 4th century BC, until 330 BC
taken by Alexander the Great in 330 BC; palaces destroyed by fire

items.description: Tomb complex of Qin Shi Huang, including the Terracotta Army pits.

P361:Q17163347.note: 'part of: lists of World Heritage Sites in Asia' — a Wikipedia list article, not a whole the mausoleum is part of.

items.name: Angkor Wat
items.description: Temple complex built by Suryavarman II, originally dedicated to Vishnu.

P571:802.note: Wikidata inception 802 CE conflicts with the documented construction under Suryavarman II (1113–1150 CE); 802 is plausibly the traditional founding year of the Khmer Empire misapplied (curator hypothesis).

time.label: constructed between 1113 and 1150 CE (reign of Suryavarman II)

items.name: Borobudur
items.description: Mahayana Buddhist monument in Central Java built under the Sailendra dynasty.

items.name: Petra

time.label: Nabataean settlement from the 4th century BC to Roman annexation in 106 AD
time.note: Only the Nabataean phase; earlier Edomite (7th c. BC+) and later Roman phases exist but are not modelled.

items.name: Masada
items.description: Herodian fortress on a plateau above the Dead Sea; last holdout of the First Jewish–Roman War.

attrs.value: 4–7 weeks; beginning around 1 March and ending in mid-April (year not stated in the abstract)
attrs.note: Logistic estimate from construction rates of the siege ramp; does not resolve the 73/74 CE question.

time.label: fall to Rome in 74 AD
time.note: Sources give '73 or 74 CE'; no rank preferred.

P2596:Q9268.action: decide whether a religion may be stated as a 'culture' facet
P2596:Q9268.note: Wikidata gives 'Judaism' (a religion) as P2596 culture. Category mismatch; GeoChronos keeps culture and religion separate.

items.name: Qumran Caves
items.description: Caves near Khirbet Qumran where the Dead Sea Scrolls were found.

period.note: 'the first traces of occupation are from the Chalcolithic period then onward to the Arab period' — period only, no numeric date in the source.

function.note: Patrich: the caves 'did not serve as habitations ... but rather as stores and hiding places' (as summarised by Wikipedia).
Broshi & Eshel believed some caves served as dwellings (Dead Sea Discoveries 6, 1999, as cited by Wikipedia).
